explanations: leave() runs at the store's default snapshot isolation. Two concurrent leaves both read a snapshot in which two doctors are on call, so both pass the cover check. Each then writes only its own entry. Their write sets don't overlap, so snapshot isolation commits both, and the shift ends up empty. This is write skew: a rule that spans several rows, checked against data that another transaction changes at the same time. Running leave() as serializable makes the commit also check the scanned shift prefix. The second transaction fails with a serialization error, gets retried, sees only one doctor left, and is refused.
